text:
sara: FYI we just got a high-priority support ticket — customer 'NimblePay' reports 3x p95 and ~6x p99 on text-generation endpoints after today's runtime rollout. Affects region us-east-1, route /v1/generate, traffic cohort 'cohort-B'. stack traces attached to the ticket. Canaries show the same pattern. :eyes:

deploy-bot: Deployment r2.8.3 -> canary-cohort-B started at 2026-03-16T09:02:00Z (triggered by release/ops).

marc: Can you paste the observability links and a couple of sample request ids? Also which config changed in the rollout (kernel selector / quant / scheduler)?

sara: Observability: https://console.redwood/instruments/obs?view=cohort-B-0326
Sample request ids: req_18a7f1, req_18a7f2, req_18a7f9
Rolled: runtime image r2.8.3 (diff from r2.8.2: kernel selector tweak, default late-binding=true, quant encoding path updated to new int8 fallback). No config changes to batching.

jin: Noting pattern: p95 jumps +3x, p99 tail is much larger. Early suspicion = cold KV cache + late-binding path interacting with new quant fallback. Can we repro one of the samples locally? share a curl with headers.

sara: repro (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: req_18a7f1" \
  -d '{"model":"open-llm-small","input":"summarize: ..."}'
```
Also attached full trace: https://console.redwood/traces/18a7f1

ellie: Can we capture pprof/flamegraph from a canary pod for a sample slow request? I can enable debug-sample-mode and rotate it off after we have captures. Need a pod name and a time window.

sara: Pod: runtime-canary-7b9f; slow window 2026-03-16T09:05:12Z -> 09:06:40Z. Command we'll run: `rdctl debug capture --pod runtime-canary-7b9f --trace-ids req_18a7f1 --duration 2m`

infra-bot: debug-sample-mode enabled on runtime-canary-7b9f by ellie (ticket 4521). TTL 10m.

jin: From preliminary trace capture: big stalls inside `quant_fallback_dispatch()` and a burst of page faults hitting `mmap` sections; KV lookup shows ~60% cache misses for that cohort on new runtime. Stack snippet: `quant_fallback_dispatch -> dispatch_kernel -> small_alloc -> futex_wait` — looks like allocation/backpressure causing tail. Sending a small annotated trace snippet.

marc: Two quick mitigations we can try in parallel: 1) shift canary traffic back to 80/20 (old:new) to reduce customer impact, 2) toggle late-binding=false for the canary runtime to force earlier kernel selection and warm-up. Both low-risk and should be quick. Thoughts?

ellie: Agreed. I'll start traffic-split change and toggle flag in canary deployment group. Will monitor p95/p99. If that recovers, we can bisect kernel selector changes.

sara: Please also capture `kvcache.*` metrics for cohort-B — we saw a coldstart spike (kvcache.miss_rate ~0.6). Might be related to eviction policy after rollout.

deploy-bot: Traffic-split for service runtime-api updated: canary-cohort-B: old:r2.8.2=80%, new:r2.8.3=20% at 2026-03-16T09:14:05Z.

infra-bot: Config patch applied: `runtime.late_binding=false` for deployment runtime-canary-7b9f by ellie.

marc: Early numbers (5m after change): cohort-B p95 down ~40%, p99 down ~55% relative to spike but not fully baseline yet. kvcache miss still elevated but trending down. Good sign.

jin: We should still plan a bisect: two variables (kernel selector tweak vs quant int8 fallback). Plan: generate N=10 micro-rollouts toggling kernel selector back/forward and run synthetic traffic with mixed sequence lengths to measure tail. Also reproducible offline using local test harness (synth token distribution). I can own the bisect if someone helps with the traffic script.

ellie: I'll keep oncall in the loop. Marking this as P1 until we confirm post-rollback stability.

sara: Customer update draft: "We've detected a latency regression affecting some requests in your cohort after a runtime update. We've partially shifted traffic back and implemented a mitigatory toggle; metrics are improving. We're performing a targeted investigation and will update with findings and next steps." OK to send?

marc: send it, mention ETA for full root-cause ~2-4 hours and that we'll follow up with a postmortem.

infra-bot: Rollback action executed: canary runtime image r2.8.2 restored for all cohort-B pods at 2026-03-16T09:32:10Z (automated rollback via release-controller).

deploy-bot: Rollforward prevented — new rollouts gated while incident is active.

ellie: Confirming the metrics after full rollback: p95 back within 10% of baseline, p99 back within 15% of baseline. nvprof traces show quant fallback not invoked under r2.8.2.

jin: From captured traces + pprof: root cause is interaction between the new kernel selector and quant fallback path when kvcache cold misses spike — leads to allocation hotspots and futex contention. Not a single kernel bug, but a combination of heuristics that cause late allocation on the hot path.

marc: Action items: (1) revert kernel-selector tweak in the next patch (cherry-pick to r2.8.2 branch), (2) add a canary test that simulates KV coldstart + mixed sequence lengths, (3) add a runtime flag to throttle quant_fallback allocations, (4) postmortem and customer write-up. Jin + Marc to own #1 and #3, Ellie to own #2, Sara to handle customer comms and support ticket closure.

sara: I'll update the support ticket and post the customer note. Thanks everyone. I'll schedule a postmortem invite for 2026-03-16T15:00Z.

ellie: Adding incident channel #incident-1785432100 and linking pager rota.

marc: Follow-up: long-term we should add a kvcache-warmup step into the rollout job (pre-warm keys for canary cohorts) — low cost and would avoid coldstart spikes.

sara: Noted. Closing the immediate thread; continuing bisect work in a separate thread.
